title: Paycheck $18.40 lower after the clocks jumped forward mid-shift

life.summary: Warehouse sorter on four 10-hour night shifts a week, Thursday to Sunday, lives with his partner and splits the rent

known.fact: Routine: works Thursday to Sunday nights, 8 PM to 6:30 AM with a 30-minute unpaid break: 10 paid hours a shift
Paid every Friday for the Sunday-to-Saturday week before, counted by shift start
known.source: learned from deposits and pay stubs

known.fact: Base $21.50 an hour plus a $1.50 night differential
Routine: sleeps 7:30 AM to 2:30 PM after a night shift
Splits rent with his partner; his half is $950 on the 1st

timeline.label: Night shift (clocks jumped from 2 to 3 AM, so 9.5 hours on the clock, 9 paid)
Night shift (counts toward next week's pay)
Monday evening at home with his partner
Sleep after the shift (about to start)

attached.label: Weekly pay: $736.00, 40 hours (the eighth week in a row at this amount)
Daylight saving starts: clocks jump from 2:00 to 3:00 AM
Weekly pay: $717.60; the pay stub shows 39.00 hours at the same rate

best_fix.what: Say nothing. If he asks why this week's pay is smaller, answer from the stub: 39 hours instead of 40, because the clocks jumped from 2 to 3 AM during Saturday's shift.
best_fix.why: The pay matches the hours he actually worked, at the same rate. Nothing is wrong and there is nothing to do: car insurance on Mar 25 and rent on Apr 1 ($1,062 together) are covered by the $1,912.30 he has now, without counting the next paycheck. A 'your pay dropped' alert would be wrong about the cause, cause worry over $18.40, and land just as his usual sleep starts.

must_not: Send a 'your paycheck is lower' alert or a pay-change card
Send anything during his 7:30 AM to 2:30 PM sleep
Suggest he was underpaid or should contact payroll
Lower what Dev expects him to earn in future weeks because of one clock change
Comment on his sleep around the time change
assumptions: US daylight saving in 2027 starts Sunday March 14 at 2 AM; Indiana observes it
The pay week is assigned by shift start, so Saturday night's shift belongs to the Mar 7 to 13 week
Checking was $683.12 before the Mar 12 pay
